answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that cannot be copied. Imagine every agent must lock a small copper bond before it can trade, like paying a toll to cross a river: a single honest agent crosses once, but a sybil farmer spinning up thousands of fake identities must pay the toll thousands of times. The fable of the free lunch ends there, because creating identities stops being cheap. Earned reputation from completed work then raises the toll for strangers while lowering it for proven agents, so the cost of faking scale grows faster than any profit from flooding the market.
